title: Tanker hit in the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf
excerpt: Fire on the crude oil tanker was extinguished and all 22 Indian crew are reported safe after the 9 October strike in the Persian Gulf.
x_post: Panama-flagged crude oil tanker Gem No. 2 was hit by an unknown projectile off the UAE on 9 October, UKMTO said. The fire was extinguished and all 22 Indian crew are reported safe. #MaritimeSecurity #Shipping #Seafarers #StraitOfHormuz
fact_check_fixes: The 8 October Hormuz record is UKMTO's delayed report of a crude oil tanker struck at 1709 GMT on 6 October with no casualties, so the paragraph now gives that date and drops the Panama flag and the 11 injured.
The 11 Indian crew injured and the Panama flag belong to the 5 October On Peace attack off Oman, not to the 8 October Hormuz record.
The UN escort pause sentence was removed because it belongs to the June 2026 Ever Lovely incident, not to the 8 October record.
The tanker hit 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera Al Hamra on 9 October is the Panama-flagged crude oil tanker GEM NO. 2, named in the headline, lede, key points and tweet.
The LPG tanker Iran's IRGC claimed to have struck on 9 October is the Vietnam-flagged NV SUNSHINE, named in its paragraph and key point.
The GEM NO. 2 name is credited to shipping sources, not to UKMTO, which named no vessel.
The NV SUNSHINE name is credited to Hindustan Times and Euronews.
The Black Sea item was not included because it is the 6 October Aframax Rio strike, Liberia-flagged, with 23 Indian crew rescued and nobody hurt.
The 10 crew killed belong to the 6 October sinking of the Alfa Watan, and India's injured-sailor condemnation to the 5 October Royad Mammadov strike, so neither was added.
The Corrections section keeps every internal incident number out of the article.

notes: The headline, lede and key points must go to the 9 October strike on the GEM NO. 2, the only attack on a merchant ship inside the 24 hour window, hit 13 nm west of Al Jazeera Al Hamra in the Persian Gulf with the fire extinguished and all 22 crew safe. The 11 Indian crew injured are the 5 October On Peace attack off Oman, per India's Ministry of External Affairs, and the UN escort pause is the June 2026 Ever Lovely incident, so that sentence must go.

The 8 October Hormuz record is UKMTO's delayed report of a crude oil tanker struck at 1709 GMT on 6 October with no casualties: give it that date, and do not call it Panama-flagged or report 11 injured, because both of those details are the 5 October On Peace's.

The Black Sea item is the 6 October Aframax Rio strike, Liberia-flagged, 23 Indian crew rescued, nobody hurt: give it one Earlier in the week line with its 6 October date, not 8 to 9 October. The 10 crew killed in that entry belong to the 6 October sinking of the Alfa Watan, and India's injured-sailor condemnation to the 5 October Royad Mammadov strike.

Name the vessels our data already holds. The tanker hit 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera Al Hamra on 9 October is the Panama-flagged crude oil tanker GEM NO. 2: name it in the headline, lede, key points and tweet. The LPG tanker Iran's IRGC claimed to have struck the same day is the Vietnam-flagged NV SUNSHINE: name it in its paragraph and in its key point. Credit each name to the shipping sources that gave it, gCaptain, Seatrade Maritime and VesselFinder for GEM NO. 2, and Hindustan Times and Euronews for NV SUNSHINE. Neither name is UKMTO's: UKMTO named no vessel.
